subject.title: In-turn background work (Workflow / run_in_background / Workflow-backed skills) is SIGKILLed at the turn boundary under the claude-cli runtime

question: Should claude-cli remain a conservative fallback that refuses unsupported background/Workflow promises, or should OpenClaw add a durable claude-cli background host and completion-delivery contract?
rationale: Current main has a narrow native-tool denylist, but the remaining Workflow-backed survival and delivery behavior crosses CLI backend, agent runtime, and channel/session ownership boundaries.

options.title: Refuse and route unsupported background work
options.body: Extend the conservative claude-cli boundary so every unsupported native or Workflow-backed background affordance is denied or redirected to ACP/OpenClaw-managed longwork with clear user-visible behavior.

options.title: Build durable claude-cli longwork
options.body: Add a persistent/detached claude-cli longwork host with origin snapshot, durable completion queue, and live proof across concurrent sessions.

options.title: Document unsupported only
options.body: Leave runtime behavior mostly as-is and document that claude-cli is not a background-work harness, accepting that reachable unsupported affordances must be manually avoided.

recommendation.title: Refuse and route unsupported background work
recommendation.body: Extend the conservative claude-cli boundary so every unsupported native or Workflow-backed background affordance is denied or redirected to ACP/OpenClaw-managed longwork with clear user-visible behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Most recent current-main owner for the claude live-session and adjacent subagent delivery surfaces that frame this product/runtime boundary.
